title: Instruments
summary: Configure analyzer connections and result-file intake for registered instruments.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Register analyzer creates an instrument connection. Open its panel to inspect the connection, enabled state and listener or folder status. Network connections use an allowed-address list; result-file instruments can use manual loading or a chosen watched folder.

Connection changes restart the affected listeners, and the outcome appears in the panel. A watched folder belongs to its instrument. Files already present when it is selected are not automatically loaded, while later eligible files are read while the application is open.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Use the laboratory’s approved connection details. Confirm instrument identity and the intended source before enabling intake. Keep one instrument’s exports in its dedicated folder and preserve the files as produced.

Connection setup is separate from service readiness and result-source approval in Bench setup. The application must remain open for listeners and folder intake to operate, including when nobody is signed in.

sections.title: If you cannot continue
paragraphs: Inspect the returned listener or folder status after a change. A saved setting does not prove a working connection or successfully processed results. Check Result imports for processing outcomes and Bench setup for missing source approval.

pages.title: Analyzer connections and watched result folders
pages.purpose: Register analyzers, match their actual communication settings, and control automatic receipt of result messages or result files.
pages.access: Manage configuration is required to register, edit, enable or disable an analyzer and choose or clear a result folder. Registration does not approve the analyzer for clinical service or supply source mappings.

fields.name: Find analyzers
fields.meaning: Locate an existing connection before registering another.
fields.values: Text matching analyzer code or name; blank shows all.
fields.rules: Optional directory filter. Open a row to see its settings and available actions.

fields.name: Code
fields.meaning: Permanent identifier for this analyzer in receipts and configuration.
fields.values: Letters, digits, period, underscore or hyphen.
fields.rules: Required at registration; 1–64 characters and unique. This screen does not rename a saved analyzer code.

fields.name: Name
fields.meaning: Readable analyzer label for laboratory staff.
fields.rules: Required at registration; at most 128 bytes and not whitespace only.

fields.name: Connection
fields.meaning: Select the supported transport and message profile.
fields.values: Network (ASTM over TCP/IP); Serial port (ASTM); AU400 / AU640 — network bridge; AU400 / AU640 — serial port; Result files.
fields.rules: Required. New connections start empty; Edit connection starts from the saved values. Changing away from Result files removes its watched-folder association.

fields.name: Listening / Folder pickup
fields.meaning: Choose whether automatic receipt starts for this connection.
fields.values: Listen for this analyzer or Keep disabled for now for message transports; Pick up files once a folder is chosen or Keep disabled for now for result files.
fields.rules: Required on registration. Enabled result-file pickup also requires a chosen readable folder. The saved Listening value is configuration, not proof that a listener successfully started.

fields.name: Listen on address
fields.meaning: Local laboratory-computer IP address on which the LIS accepts analyzer or bridge connections.
fields.values: One IPv4 or IPv6 loopback, private/unique-local, or link-local address.
fields.rules: Required for network connections. Wildcard and public addresses are refused. Use an address assigned to this computer; a valid-looking address can still fail to bind.

fields.name: Port
fields.meaning: Local network port used by this analyzer listener.
fields.rules: Required for network connections. A configured listener endpoint cannot be shared by another analyzer; another program using the port can also prevent startup.

fields.name: Analyzer addresses allowed to connect
fields.meaning: Restrict which source IP addresses may open this listener.
fields.values: One or more allowed IPv4 or IPv6 loopback, private/unique-local, or link-local addresses, separated by commas or whitespace.
fields.rules: Required for network connections; duplicate addresses are refused. For an AU network bridge use the bridge’s source address. This list is a network restriction, not cryptographic proof of analyzer identity.

fields.name: Serial port
fields.meaning: Operating-system device connected to the analyzer.
fields.values: An actual local serial device, such as COM3 or /dev/ttyUSB0.
fields.rules: Required for serial connections; nonblank, no control characters, at most 1024 bytes. Another analyzer cannot use the same configured device.

fields.name: Baud rate
fields.meaning: Serial transmission speed that must match the analyzer or bridge.
fields.values: ASTM: whole number from 1 to 4,000,000. AU400 / AU640: 2400, 4800 or 9600.
fields.rules: Required for serial connections. A permitted number does not prove the local adapter supports that rate.

fields.name: Data bits
fields.meaning: Number of data bits per serial character.
fields.rules: Required for serial connections; match the actual device configuration.

fields.name: Parity
fields.meaning: Serial parity check used by the device.
fields.rules: Required for serial connections; do not infer it from the cable or analyzer name.

fields.name: Stop bits
fields.meaning: Serial stop-bit count.
fields.rules: Required for serial connections.

fields.name: Transmission class
fields.meaning: AU framing acknowledgement behavior.
fields.values: Class A — no acknowledgements; Class B — ACK / NAK.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections; copy the authorized online parameter sheet. The LIS acknowledges Class B receipt only after durable receipt.

fields.name: Start code (hex)
fields.meaning: AU control byte or pair that begins a frame.
fields.values: One or two hexadecimal bytes from 01 through 1F, excluding 06 and 15; separate two bytes with whitespace.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. Enter the analyzer’s configured sequence, for example 02 only when that is its actual setting.

fields.name: End code (hex)
fields.meaning: AU control byte or pair that ends a frame.
fields.values: One or two hexadecimal bytes from 01 through 1F, excluding 06 and 15.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. ETB intermediate endings take effect only when the configured end is the single byte 03.

fields.name: BCC checksum used
fields.meaning: Whether each AU frame contains the one-byte XOR block-check character.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. Match the parameter sheet; the application does not guess this value.

fields.name: ETB block endings used
fields.meaning: Whether intermediate AU blocks use ETB before the final block.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. Applies only with the single-byte ETX end code 03.

fields.name: Maximum block length
fields.meaning: Maximum complete AU wire-frame size.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections; includes start/end control bytes and any checksum.

fields.name: Frame receive timeout (ms)
fields.meaning: Maximum wait while receiving the current AU frame.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections; match the analyzer’s timing settings.

fields.name: Next block timeout (ms)
fields.meaning: Maximum wait for the next AU block in a multi-block message.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections; match the analyzer’s timing settings.

fields.name: Instrument unit number sent
fields.meaning: Whether incoming AU result headers contain a two-digit unit number.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections; describes the incoming format rather than assigning a new analyzer identity.

fields.name: Rack number width
fields.meaning: Width of the incoming AU rack field.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. Cup position is present when a rack number is sent and absent when it is not sent.

fields.name: Sample ID width
fields.meaning: Width of the AU specimen barcode field.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. Match the actual message width; a zero-width sample identifier is unsupported.

fields.name: Result field width
fields.meaning: Width of an AU raw result value.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. This is field length, not decimal precision; the two flag characters are separate.

fields.name: Sex field sent
fields.meaning: Whether normal AU patient messages include the one-character sex field.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections. This configures parsing; it does not infer a patient’s sex.

fields.name: Age field sent
fields.meaning: Whether normal AU patient messages include the three-character age field.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections.

fields.name: Month field sent
fields.meaning: Whether normal AU patient messages include the two-character month field.
fields.rules: Required for AU connections.

fields.name: Patient information 1–6 width
fields.meaning: Exact width of each of the six optional AU patient-information fields.
fields.values: Six independent whole numbers, each from 0 to 20 characters.
fields.rules: All six values are required for AU connections. Enter 0 separately for each field not sent. The LIS preserves these as incoming fields; this setting does not assign clinical meaning.

fields.name: Watched folder
fields.meaning: Dedicated local folder from which this analyzer’s result files are automatically received.
fields.values: An existing readable directory chosen with the operating system’s folder dialog; No folder chosen when unset.
fields.rules: Available only for Result files. A folder can belong to only one analyzer. The saved absolute path is read-only here; use Choose folder or Change folder.

fields.name: Folder pickup status
fields.meaning: Current observation of automatic file pickup.
fields.values: Checking; Status unavailable; Disabled; Watching; Error or a detailed failure message.
fields.rules: Read-only. Warnings report files waiting more than five minutes and oversized files. Status depends on the running app; the saved enabled switch alone does not prove successful pickup.

fields.name: Files already in the folder
fields.meaning: Count of files found when the folder was chosen.
fields.values: Nonnegative count in the folder-selection result.
fields.rules: Read-only. Those existing files form the starting baseline and are not loaded automatically. Load any intended existing file explicitly through Result imports.

actions.name: Register analyzer
actions.does: Open the connection form and save a new analyzer. The wide form groups its fields under Analyzer and Connection, plus AU framing and timing, AU sample and result fields and AU optional patient fields for an AU400/AU640 connection; Register analyzer and Cancel stay at the bottom while the fields scroll.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration; unique Code, Name and all required settings for the chosen connection.
actions.result: Creates the versioned connection. Message listeners are restarted; the result reports whether restart succeeded. Result-file connections need a folder for automatic pickup.

actions.name: Open row / Previous / Next / Close
actions.does: Inspect saved connection settings and move through analyzers.
actions.result: The analyzer panel opens without changing connection or service status.

actions.name: Edit connection / Save connection
actions.does: Replace the selected analyzer’s communication settings. The form uses the same sections as Register analyzer, without Analyzer.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration and the current saved revision.
actions.result: The new revision is saved and message listeners are restarted. Review the feedback for startup failure before relying on receipt.

actions.name: Enable listening / Disable listening
actions.does: Start or stop automatic message receipt for a configured analyzer.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration; the enable-confirmation dialog is accepted.
actions.result: Saves the enabled state and restarts all analyzer listeners. An analyzer sending during the restart may need to resend.

actions.name: Enable folder pickup / Disable folder pickup
actions.does: Control automatic receipt of new files from a chosen folder.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration and a Result files connection.
actions.result: Saves the enabled state. Disabling automatic pickup does not prevent authorized manual loading through Result imports.

actions.name: Choose folder / Change folder
actions.does: Select a dedicated directory and establish its existing-file baseline.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration, Result files connection, readable folder not assigned to another analyzer.
actions.result: Automatic pickup considers new files after they stop changing. Existing files are counted but not automatically loaded; close the result notice after reviewing it.

actions.name: Clear folder
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration and a currently chosen folder.
actions.result: Automatic pickup stops for that folder; saved receipts and imports remain. This action does not delete the files.

actions.name: Cancel
actions.does: Close an unsaved registration, connection or enable dialog.
actions.availableWhen: A dialog is open and no save is underway.
actions.result: Keeps the existing saved connection. A native folder-picker cancellation selects no replacement.

restrictions: Connection registration, source mappings, method approval, and instrument service readiness are separate. Review the relevant Bench setup and Result imports guidance before expecting received data to be usable.

AU support here covers result reception. Automatic test requisition (TRI) lookup is unavailable. Copy all format settings from the laboratory’s authorized analyzer configuration; do not invent a profile.
Automatic folder pickup operates only while the application is open, including its sign-in screen. It never moves or deletes source files.
A receipt or transport acknowledgement is not proof that a result was matched, imported or accepted. Follow the receipt and import status through Result imports.

Saving connection or enabled-state changes restarts analyzer listeners. Coordinate with laboratory operations so interrupted transmissions can be reconciled. Choosing or clearing a folder is picked up by the folder watcher without requiring that listener restart.
This screen retains analyzer records; it has no delete or rename workflow. Configuration changes require the latest revision.
workflow: Search for the analyzer and inspect any existing configuration before registering another.
Choose the exact supported transport and enter the device’s actual address, serial and, when applicable, AU format settings.
Save and check both the saved configuration and listener-startup feedback.
For result files, choose a dedicated folder and review the existing-file count. Load intended baseline files manually through Result imports.

Complete the laboratory’s required source mappings and service-readiness checks, then inspect receipts/imports to establish that the intended synthetic or authorized validation input followed the expected path.

troubleshooting.problem: Connection or code is already in use
troubleshooting.recovery: Inspect the registered analyzers and correct the intended Code, network endpoint or serial device. Do not create a near-duplicate analyzer merely to bypass the conflict.

troubleshooting.problem: Settings saved but a listener could not start
troubleshooting.recovery: Read the restart feedback, verify the local IP, port/device ownership and operating-system access, then correct the connection. Reconcile any transmissions that occurred during the interruption.

troubleshooting.problem: An AU message is rejected or remains incomplete
troubleshooting.recovery: Compare every framing, timing and field-width setting with the authorized analyzer parameter sheet. Inspect the durable receipt/import failure; do not change clinical values to make the message parse.

troubleshooting.problem: Files are not appearing in Result imports
troubleshooting.recovery: Check that the app is open, pickup is enabled, the folder is readable and the file is new and no longer changing. Existing files at folder selection need manual loading; waiting or oversized warnings need investigation.

troubleshooting.problem: Folder is already watched by another analyzer
troubleshooting.recovery: Choose the correct analyzer’s configuration or select a dedicated folder. Two analyzer identities cannot watch the same directory.

troubleshooting.problem: Save reports that the analyzer changed
troubleshooting.recovery: Reload the record and review its latest settings before repeating the edit or enable action.
